A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same capacity-gap law and MiniMA/MiniChat work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPT2/Pythia distillation experiments, MiniMA benchmark and ablation results, and MiniChat automated and human assessments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and reports additional teacher-model, compression-baseline, and ablation results in Tables 2 and 4.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains gradient-based structured pruning, the same sparsity decomposition, the equally weighted teacher-label and ground-truth cross-entropy loss, and MiniMA's symmetric pruning with bottom/top layer removal. Additional teachers and ablation variants do not replace or add components to the default method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same English, Chinese, coding, language-modeling, reasoning, and instruction-following coverage. OpenWebText, the Pile/GitHub/WuDao mixture, instruction data, and all benchmark datasets remain. Additional teacher configurations and reduced-token LAMBADA results do not introduce a distinct task or population.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated ShortGPT and LayerChop compression comparators in Table 2 and patient knowledge distillation in Table 4. The earlier broad model comparisons remain in Appendix F. The 126B-token ShearedLLaMA row reproduces v2's no-distillation row under a different label; it should not be counted as wholly new evidence.

E3.justification: v4 expands the teacher configurations to LLaMA2-70B and LLaMA3.1-8B and adds a 252B-token ShearedLLaMA condition intended to match MiniMA's compute. Table 2 explicitly identifies a larger corpus for the LLaMA3.1 run. Existing benchmark metrics, prompting protocols, and splits remain unchanged; omitted pilot settings do not establish changed training.

E4.justification: v4 adds layer-dropping and patient-knowledge ablations, extends teacher-size sensitivity to 70B, and adds reduced-token LAMBADA curves. The reduced-token WikiText2 analysis already existed in v2 Appendix B and is incorporated into Figure 3. The standalone shopping case is removed, while comparative coding/writing cases and human-assessment analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 3.5 and Figure 4 newly report R² = 0.9957 for the existing linear fit, adding a goodness-of-fit statistic. This does not establish additional runs or uncertainty estimation. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval documentation, or significance tests are supplied.

E6.justification: Substantial new result entries cover additional teachers, compression baselines, ablations, and reduced-token LAMBADA evaluation. For example, the newly reported 70B-teacher student scores 26.91 on MMLU, and the LLaMA3.1 student scores 31.72. These are additional configurations, not improvements to the retained MiniMA result of 28.51. Original broad benchmarks, chat scores, human ratings, and most appendix results remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 removes v2 Table 1's analytical FLOP and memory bounds for teacher assistants and MiniMoE. The pruning/distillation equations, capacity-law coefficients, corollary, and general training-compute formulas remain. Proposition 1 and the parameterized fitting equation largely formalize existing content; no new mathematical proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine the central bottleneck. v2 emphasizes the difficulty of combining a large teacher, good student performance, and little additional compute. v4 instead emphasizes expensive searches for the optimal teacher at a specified student size and claims the law eliminates that search overhead. The linear relationship and practical distillation contribution remain.

C2.justification: Remark 1 and Section 4.3 extend interpretations to pruning and distillation-objective robustness. The limitations newly acknowledge that data scale, mixture, and distillation techniques are not core scaling factors in the analysis. Some new wording overstates the evidence: Table 2's MMLU and DROP scores increase slightly from the 13B-teacher student to the 70B-teacher student despite the claimed consistent degradation.

D1.justification: v4 removes the pilot-distillation implementation paragraph specifying 512-token sequences, batch size, optimizer settings, schedule, training duration, clipping, and hardware. It also replaces the explicit approximately 90% intermediate-checkpoint description with unspecified fewer tokens. These omissions materially reduce reproducibility of the central law experiment. Large-model adaptation/finetuning details and code/model access references largely remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to ShortGPT, LLaMA 3, Apple foundation models, Gemma 2, and Muralidharan et al.'s pruning/distillation work, while removing Rae et al.'s Gopher reference. It newly positions recent distilled models as consistent with the proposed teacher-size relationship. The main related-work background remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized into overview, method, setup, observations, and characterization; Section 4 now separates shared setup, main results, and ablations instead of organizing primarily by MiniMA/MiniChat. Appendices are reordered and consolidated, and authorship and affiliation text changes.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. The original combined curse/law figure is split and redrawn, the triangle labels change, and pilot plots are consolidated into an expanded six-panel figure. Broad benchmark tables are merged in Appendix F, the main comparison table is redesigned, and the original overhead and shopping-case tables are removed.

improvement.justification: The added compression comparisons with comparable compute budgets, larger-teacher test, and pruning/objective ablations strengthen the practical efficiency evidence beyond v2's broad model comparisons. The reorganized exposition also makes that evidence easier to assess. The net gain is limited by missing pilot-training and checkpoint details and by generality and monotonicity claims stronger than the added tests justify.
